verdict.rationale: Airweave's own quickstart documents running it yourself: clone the public GitHub repo, run ./start.sh, and open the dashboard on localhost, on macOS, Linux or WSL. A community comment also places it in the open-source space. However, the evidence covers only local deployment, not production self-hosting on infrastructure you control. missing for 10: explicit Docker/Docker Compose documentation, production or server/Kubernetes self-host guidance (scaling, configuration, persistence), explicit open-source license confirmation, independent hands-on self-host corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can self-host the memory layer from open-source code (e.g. via Docker) on infrastructure I control

citations.quote: If you prefer to run Airweave yourself, you can deploy it locally on macOS, Linux or WSL.
After cloning the repository and starting the server, you will be able to open the dashboard at http://localhost:8080
Always great to have more innovation in the open source AI space
